chunks: He said: And Husayn ibn Ali ibn Ma'mar narrated to me from his father from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

and mentioned Bada (divine change of decree) for Allah, so he said: That which Allah brought forth to the angels, and the angels brought forth to the messengers, and the messengers brought forth to the human beings, is not Bada; and among the definite matters is that this son of mine is the Qaim.

key_terms.الرُّسُل: The messengers: Prophets who receive revelation from angels.
key_terms.الْبَدَاء: Bada: The doctrine of divine change of decree or manifestation of God's will at different times.
key_terms.الْقَائِم: The Qaim: The Mahdi, the awaited leader who will rise to establish justice.
key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَة: The angels: Divine beings who receive and convey God's commands.
key_terms.الْمُحْتَم: Al-Muhtam: The definite or inevitable matter, as opposed to Bada.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Bada and definite divine decree in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that the progressive revelation of divine knowledge through angels, prophets, and humans constitutes a natural transmission of information rather than 'Bada' (divine alteration of destiny). He distinguishes this from specific, immutable decrees, citing the emergence of his son as the Qaim as a definitive, non-negotiable event. This distinction serves to refute the Waqifiya, who often misinterpreted Bada as implying uncertainty in the Imamate, by affirming that while some matters are subject to divine change, the identity of the Qaim is fixed.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 42 - Narrated to me Husain bin Ali bin Muammar from his father from Abdullah bin Sinan that: I heard from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said with regard to change of destiny (Bada) by Allah:

That which Almighty Allah gave to the angels, they conveyed it to the prophets and the prophets in turn conveyed to the people [law of religion]. Therefore, in this instance it is not Bada, because it is called definite (Mahtum); and among the definite matters is that this son of mine is the Qaim.
